extracted.intended_audience: general news readers and media professionals interested in journalism ethics
extracted.subtask_description: A news report describing a case in which a staff journalist fabricated parts of multiple stories, the ensuing internal investigation, and the responses by the magazine and other outlets. Useful for understanding media-ethics failures and institutional responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and honesty in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Claas Relotius falsified his articles on a grand scale and even invented characters, deceiving both readers and his colleagues; he admitted to partial fabrications in at least 14 of nearly 60 articles, including making up dialogue and quotes and creating composite characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not fabricate facts, sources, dialogue, quotes, or invent characters; such fabrication can lead to resignation/firing, retraction/review of stories, and stripping of awards. Examples of wrongdoing noted: invented characters, made up dialogue and quotes, created composite characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal investigation and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: After suspicions were raised, Der Spiegel carried out an internal investigation and said it is still combing through the allegations against Relotius and will set up a commission made up of people from both inside and outside the company to investigate his work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations should investigate alleged falsification, review the reporter's body of work, and convene independent or mixed commissions to audit reporting when large-scale fabrication is suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency to readers about suspected forgery
rubrics_metrics.description: For now, Relotius' stories will be left unaltered online, but with a notification telling readers that his reporting is under suspicion of extensive forgery and manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investigation is ongoing, publish clear notifications on suspect articles to inform readers while vetting; balancing preservation of the record with transparent disclosure of concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and due diligence by other publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: Other publications that published Relotius' work (e.g., Frankfurter Allgemeine Sonntagszeitung, S√ºddeutsche Zeitung Magazin, Financial Times Deutschland) said they were reviewing the stories he had published; some reported no evidence yet of forgery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers who discover a contributor fabricated material should review previously published pieces, report findings, and take corrective action as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for awards and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The CNN Journalist Awards (for which Relotius had won in 2014) were reviewed by the awards jury, which voted unanimously to strip Relotius of both awards after Der Spiegel went public with its investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarding bodies and juries may revoke honors if recipients are found to have falsified work; such revocation is a concrete consequence of verified misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional reputational impact and precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: The scandal is described as a heavy blow to Der Spiegel, a publication renowned for quality journalism; the article cites past high-profile fabrication scandals (Jayson Blair at The New York Times, Stephen Glass at The New Republic) as precedents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fabrication damages public trust and institutional reputation; organizations should be aware of historical precedents and the long-term consequences of failing to detect misconduct.
